name: VCSL Pipe Organ (music-production build)
comment: Built from the Pipe Organ of the Versilian Community Sample Library (VCSL) by Versilian Studios, CC0 1.0; the organ was sampled by Simon Dalzell of Ivy Audio, and the folder's Info.txt encourages crediting both. Source: https://github.com/sgossner/VCSL at c1ea7bcc3c7309650ab0da9d15c9cd1fbc4a4c7e. A pipe organ sampled every minor third, three presets: the full manual registration Man3Open (program 19), a soft stopped-flute manual Man3Quiet (bank 1) and the pedal division (bank 2). Each key was held about 10 s; build b2 cuts a loop from each recording's steady part (2 to 9.6 s after the onset, clear of key noises), matched in phase and crossfaded over 0.3 s, so a held note lasts as long as the key, and the release comes from the envelope and the mix's room. Pitches come from each recording's spectrum: both manuals sound an octave above their file names (8' pitch; the full registration adds a quieter sub-octave from about middle C up), the pedal sounds at its names (its 16' fundamental). Velocity does not change the sound, as on an organ; shape dynamics with expression (CC11), like a swell pedal. Left out: the three lowest soft-manual notes, 12-28 dB quieter than their neighbours, and the soft pedal recordings, whose level beats by 10-15 dB about once a second. Changes: the full and pedal registrations keep their recorded voicing (no levelling between notes); the soft stop's notes differ by 5-14 dB from their neighbours in the recording, so each is pulled toward its neighbours (at most 6 dB); leading silence trimmed; 16-bit TPDF dither.
copyright: Source samples CC0 1.0 (Versilian Studios VCSL; organ sampled by Simon Dalzell, Ivy Audio)
